insight: For Curaçao, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks, indicating a slight increase in performance after the pause. However, the team's approach before the break seems to impact the outcome, as they tend to struggle when pressing beforehand, losing momentum at an average rate of 0.100 minutes, and only managing to maintain their momentum once in three attempts. In contrast, when Curaçao is not pressing before the break, they tend to come out stronger, with an average gain in momentum of 0.133 minutes, suggesting that a more relaxed approach before the pause allows them to regroup and refocus. Overall, these statistics suggest that Curaçao benefits from hydration breaks, particularly when they are not exerting themselves intensely beforehand.
